com.tang EmmyLua 1.4.0 tangzx Custom Languages Support for the Lua programming language, with a JUnit-style LuaUnit test runner (tests tree, gutter icons, run/debug of cases, rerun of failed tests).

Source Code | Gitter | Donate | Doc | VSCode-EmmyLua

Features:
  • Syntax highlighting
    • Highlight global value
    • Highlight local/param value
    • Highlight up value
  • Code completion
    • Keyword completion
    • Basic completion
    • Type inferred based completion
  • Debugger
    • Attach Debugger(Windows only)
    • Remote Debugger(Mobdebug.lua)
  • Lua 5.4 support
  • Find usages
  • Rename
  • Go to definition
  • Go to symbol
  • Go to class
  • Go to file
  • Parameter name hints
  • Comment based type/class annotation
  • Structure view
  • Comment in/out
  • Color settings page
  • Method override line marker
  • Quick Documentation
  • Live templates
  • Postfix completion templates
  • Code formatter
  • Code intentions
  • Code inspections
  • Lua Standard Library/API
  • Region folding
  • Lua Check Tool
LuaUnit test running:
  • Tests tree: every case a plain lua tests/run_tests.lua run would execute has its node, grouped by manifest section, file and suite — declared cases, programmatically added cases from generator loops (id = "..."/desc = "..." rows, including rows of a shared data module), commented-out cases shown as ignored
  • Run/Debug gutter icons: in the manifest the first line runs everything, a section title line runs its group, an entry line runs that file; in the test files the icons sit on case declarations and data rows. A plain click runs the only test behind the icon, while a right click opens the menu with Run, Debug and Modify Run Configuration. A data row several suites build their cases from is more than one test: the icon asks which one to run — a labelled Run/Debug pair per generator plus a Modify Run Configuration action
  • A failed case shows an expected/actual diff (Cmd/Ctrl+D); the console hyperlinks to declaration lines, and to the data files a case reads (at fixture(path:line) frames, any type, not only .lua)
  • A run is scoped to one case, one file, one manifest section, or the whole manifest; the LuaUnit run configuration holds the interpreter, the working directory, interpreter arguments and environment variables
  • Framework frames (luaunit.lua, the runner, [C]) are stripped from failure traces, and a case's own print output goes to its node in the tree
  • Rerun Failed Tests: the failed cases re-run in one click
  • Debug Failed Tests: the failed cases re-run under the debugger (mobdebug), one suite after another; breakpoints work across same-named suite files
  • Cmd/Ctrl+C (and the context menu) copies the test name, a group name or the file's project-relative path; Copy Reference on a case declaration yields its full LuaUnit name
  • Sections of the manifest: 
    'tests/general.lua',    -- no comment above: no group

--SS7
'tests/ss7/test_decode_ss7.lua',
'tests/ss7/test_encode_ss7.lua',
  • A case is ignored by commenting it out: a commented-out data row (-- id = 'x') or a function inside a block comment stays in the tree as ignored, and luaunit.skip("reason") opts out at run time
  • A case's description — shown next to its name in the tree — is the free -- ... line above the declaration or the data row, or the row's trailing comment; the same rule serves active and ignored cases
  • An "All tests" run configuration is created and selected automatically the first time a project with a LuaUnit manifest is opened — just press Run
